fixes.explanation: Elihu is the one speaking here, and he says it plainly: "For the ear tests words as the mouth tastes food." (Job 34:3) So you don't just swallow every word that comes by. You check it first. I never send out a batch without sampling the dough, and Elihu wants the same care with words.

That's it, baker. Elihu has Job saying he is righteous and that God has deprived him of justice (Job 34:5). Notice this is Elihu reporting Job's words, not Job speaking. Elihu is about to push back, and his next move is to say that it is far from God to do wrong (Job 34:10).
I see why you'd think that, baker. But in this verse the complaint Elihu quotes is aimed at God: "…God has deprived me of justice." (Job 34:5) Job's friends aren't the ones named here.
Nope, riches don't come into this verse at all, baker. The thing Elihu says Job claims has no profit is delighting in God (Job 34:9). Riches never get named in it.

Wealth isn't what Elihu names, baker. Nobody judges a batch by the size of the baker's bank account, and this verse works the same way. God repays "…according to a man’s deeds…" (Job 34:11). Money never enters the picture.

Elihu says the opposite, baker. "There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide." (Job 34:22) The verse before it says God's eyes are on the ways of a man and that He sees his every step (Job 34:21). So no shadow is deep enough.
Not quite, baker. Elihu says God "…sets up others in their place." (Job 34:24) No empty chairs in that line. The verse goes straight from shattering to setting up.

Right, baker. Elihu says, "They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted." (Job 34:28) So the cry reached God, and He heard it. The verse doesn't leave that outcry unheard.
Not quite, baker. Elihu says, "You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know." (Job 34:33) The choosing goes to the "you" in that line, and he says "not I." Elihu isn't the one making this choice.
Right. Elihu says, "You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know." (Job 34:33) The choice isn't his, because he says "not I." He puts the choosing on the "you" in that line.

That's the line. Elihu says the wise men will declare, "Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight." (Job 34:35) Keep in mind this is what Elihu says they will say. I think that's a hard thing to hear about anybody.
I get why you'd think that, since Elihu is the one talking. But he says Job "…multiplies his words against God." (Job 34:37) The blank is God. And the story isn't over yet.
Close, since Elihu does talk about men all through this speech. But in the last verse he says Job "…multiplies his words against God." (Job 34:37) The blank is God. And the story isn't over yet.
